engineHelp.title: How to Use External Engine
engineHelp.intro: Connect a powerful chess engine running on your computer to Kingside for deeper analysis. Follow these steps:
engineHelp.step1Desc: Download kingside-engine-bridge for your operating system from GitHub Releases.
engineHelp.step2Desc: Install Stockfish or another UCI-compatible chess engine on your computer.
engineHelp.step3Desc: Extract the archive and run the bridge binary. It will start a WebSocket server on port 9090.
engineHelp.step4Desc: Open config.yaml (created on first run) and copy the secret_key value.
engineHelp.step5Desc: Go to any analysis page, click the ⚙ gear icon in the engine panel, and select "External Engine".
engineHelp.step6Desc: Enter the WebSocket URL and your secret key from config.yaml.
engineHelp.step7Desc: Press Connect. The status indicator will turn green when connected. Your engine is now analyzing positions!
engineHelp.faqConfigDesc: The bridge creates config.yaml on first run. Below are correct examples for each operating system. Important: secret_key must always be in quotes (otherwise YAML parse error for hex values).
engineHelp.faqSecretKeyNote: Always wrap secret_key in quotes — hex strings like 5caa... may be misinterpreted by YAML without them.
engineHelp.faqWindowsPathNote: On Windows use .\  prefix for relative paths to the engine executable.

play.title: Play Online
play.description: Challenge players worldwide in bullet, blitz, rapid or classical. Play against bots (8 levels) to practice. Custom time controls available.
play.guide:
Play against other players or bots.

Online games:
1. Go to Lobby (home page)
2. Select time control: Bullet (1-2 min), Blitz (3-5 min), Rapid (10-15 min), Classical (30+ min)
3. Or create a custom time control with any initial time and increment
4. Click "Play" — matchmaking finds an opponent of similar rating
5. During the game: move pieces by dragging or clicking. Premove is supported — make your next move while opponent is thinking
6. After the game: click "Rematch" to play again with the same opponent

Bot games:
1. In the Lobby, switch to "Play Bot" tab
2. Choose difficulty level (1-20, where 1 is beginner and 20 is Stockfish at full strength)
3. Choose your color (White, Black, or Random)
4. Choose time control
5. Click "Play"

Watch live games:
Click "Live Games" in the menu to spectate ongoing games between other players.

Challenge a friend:
Visit a player's profile and click "Challenge". Choose time control and send the challenge.

analyze.title: Deep Analysis
analyze.description: Stockfish 18 runs in your browser — no downloads needed. Connect your own engine for unlimited depth. Get accuracy scores, move classifications, and eval graphs.
analyze.guide:
Analyze any chess position with Stockfish 18.

Basic analysis:
1. Go to Workshop > New Analysis, or click "Review" after a game
2. Click "Start" to activate the engine
3. The engine shows the best move and evaluation. Use +/− buttons to change the number of lines (MultiPV, 1-10)
4. Navigate moves with arrow keys or buttons. Click on any move in the notation to jump to that position

Variations:
- Make an alternative move on the board — it creates a variation branch
- Right-click a variation to promote or delete it

Game Report:
After a finished game, click "Analyze" to get a full report:
- Accuracy percentage for both players
- Each move classified: Brilliant (!!) / Best / Good / Inaccuracy (?!) / Mistake (?) / Blunder (??)
- Eval graph showing the advantage over time

Board Editor:
Click "FEN" button to open the position editor. Place pieces freely to analyze any position.

External engines:
Click the gear icon (⚙) in the engine panel to connect a stronger engine running on your computer via Engine Bridge.

Export:
Click "↓ PGN" to download the game with your analysis and variations.

Mobile:
On mobile, the screen splits into two panels below the board. Each panel has tabs (Moves / Engine) so you can see notation and engine lines simultaneously.

puzzles.title: Puzzles & Training
puzzles.description: Solve the daily puzzle. Race against the clock in Puzzle Rush. Generate custom puzzles from any PGN — train on your own mistakes. Filter by theme: forks, pins, mates, sacrifices.
puzzles.guide:
Solve chess puzzles to improve your tactical vision.

Daily Puzzle:
A new puzzle every day. Find it on the home page or go to Daily Puzzle in the menu.

Puzzle Rush:
1. Go to Puzzle Rush in the menu
2. Choose time limit: 3 minutes or 5 minutes
3. Solve as many puzzles as possible before time runs out
4. Your best scores appear on the leaderboard

Generate Puzzles from Games:
1. Go to Puzzles (menu)
2. Click "Generate from PGN" at the top
3. Upload a .pgn file or paste PGN text
4. Open "Advanced Settings" to tune generation:
   - Depth (8-22): analysis depth, higher = better but slower
   - Lines (2-5): number of engine lines to compare
   - Gap (cp): minimum difference between best and second-best move
   - Max 2nd line (cp): skip positions where the alternative is already strong
   - Skip hanging captures: filter out trivial free-piece captures
   - Skip attacked by lesser: filter moves where the piece lands on a square attacked by a cheaper piece
   - Skip undefended after move: filter moves leaving the piece undefended
5. Click "Generate Puzzles" and wait for analysis
6. Review generated puzzles and click "Save to Server"

Solving:
The board shows the position — find the best move. After solving or failing, click "Next" for the next puzzle. Click "Analysis" to open the position in the analysis board.

workshop.title: Workshop
workshop.description: Import and manage PGN files. Save your analyses. Set up any position with the board editor.
workshop.guide:
Your personal chess workspace.

My Analyses:
Saved analyses appear here. Click any to continue where you left off. Each analysis preserves your variations and annotations.

PGN Files:
1. Go to Workshop > PGN Files
2. Click "Upload" to import a .pgn file
3. Click a file to see its games. Click a game to open it in the analysis board
4. Rename a file: click the pencil icon (✎) on the file card
5. Delete a file: click × on the file card (deletes all games inside)
6. Delete a single game: click × next to the game in the game list

broadcasts.title: Live Broadcasts
broadcasts.description: Watch top tournament games in real-time with engine analysis.
broadcasts.guide:
Watch live chess tournament games with real-time engine analysis.

1. Go to Broadcasts in the menu
2. Active tournaments appear in the list automatically
3. Click a tournament to see rounds, click a round to see games
4. Click a game to watch it live with the analysis board

social.title: Community
social.description: Add friends, see who's online, challenge them to a game. Direct messages. Real-time notifications.
social.guide:
Connect with other players.

Friends:
1. Visit a player's profile (Players page or search)
2. Click "Add Friend". They will receive a notification
3. Go to Friends page to see who's online. Online friends have a green dot
4. Click a friend's name to view their profile, or click "Challenge" to start a game

Messages:
Click the envelope icon in the header to open direct messages. Click a friend to start a conversation.

Notifications:
The bell icon in the header shows unread notifications: friend requests, challenges, game invitations. Click to view and manage.

Blocking:
On a player's profile, click "Block" to prevent them from messaging you or appearing in matchmaking.

customize.title: Personalize
customize.description: Choose your board theme. Adjust sounds and animations. Play in English or Russian.
customize.guide:
Personalize your experience.

Settings page (click your username > Settings):
- Board theme: Classic, Green, Blue, Brown
- Piece set: Standard, Cburnett, Alpha, Merida
- Notation: show/hide coordinates on the board
- Input mode: drag or click
- Sound effects: on/off
- Move animation speed
- Language: English or Russian

rating.title: Rating System
rating.guide:
Track your progress with Elo ratings.

- Separate ratings for each time control: Bullet, Blitz, Rapid, Classical, and Puzzles
- Starting rating: 1500
- Rating changes after each game based on the result and opponent's rating
- View your rating history chart on your profile page
- See other players' profiles: click their name anywhere in the app
- Players page shows all registered players sorted by rating
- Online counter in the header shows how many players are currently on the site
